text:
alex: noticing heavy queueing on ap-southeast-1 GPU pools — tail latencies spiking, some 16GB jobs hitting OOMs. grafana shows GPU util at 98% for the past 12m.

maria: seeing same, model-serving errors ~502 for a subset of endpoints. Are dedicated pools affected or just hosted?

sre-oncall: both hosted and some small dedicated pools in ap-southeast-1 are degraded. Suspect capacity evaporation after node eviction earlier (kube events show preemptions + AZ flapping).

alex: propose immediate weighted shift from ap-southeast-1 -> us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Plan: canary 10% -> 30% -> 70% over 20m, with rollback threshold on 95th p99 latency and error rate.

maria: +1. What about cache cold start? KV/prefix cache in us-west will be cold, might cause short-lived latency blips. Add traffic slow-start and pre-warm for critical routes.

jing: I can kick off cache-warm jobs for the top 50 model keys. That should shave initial token latency.

leo: recommend routing weights: ap-southeast-1 0 -> us-west-2 0.6 -> eu-west-1 0.4 to keep a lower RTT for NA customers but still bleed to EU.

alex: agreed. Also enable model-variant fallback: small-quantized for non-critical calls to reduce OOMs if node runs low. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/glb-failover

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered change request: glb-route-change by alex. Approvals required: 1.

maria: adding assertion: no simultaneous rollback of dedicated scaling during weighting or we will thrash autoscaler. Lock dedicated pool autoscaling for 30m.

alex: locking autoscale now. Command: 
```
# lock autoscaler for ap-southeast-1 dedicated pools
redwoodctl autoscale lock --pool ap-southeast-1 --duration 30m
```

sre-oncall: pre-checks done: healthchecks ok outside ap-southeast-1, spare capacity in us-west-2 shows 150 GPUs free (slots), eu-west-1 ~80 GPUs.

alex: performing canary. Executing GLB change: 
```
# weighted route update
curl -X POST "https://glb-api.internal/v1/routes/update" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GLB_TOKEN" -d '{"policy":"weighted","weights":{"ap-southeast-1":0.0,"us-west-2":0.6,"eu-west-1":0.4},"drain_seconds":120}'
```

devops-bot: glb-api: request accepted, change id 69c2. Rolling out to edge POPs.

maria: canary at 10% now, metrics look ok so far. p50 stable, p95 +30ms increase but within alerting threshold.

jing: cache warm jobs started. Warming: top 50 keys for model gpt-nano and gpt-medium.

leo: note — cross-region egress will add cost. Estimate extra egress ~$0.06/token for affected traffic until ap-southeast recovers. Flagging finance if we hold >2h.

alex: ack, will alert finance if >2h. Prioritize stability over cost.

sre-oncall: after 12m -> increasing to 30%: changing weights to us-west-2 0.6 eu-west-1 0.4 (canary already at 10 -> stepping to 30).

devops-bot: change id 69c2 updated: canary -> 30%. Edge reports: no error spike.

maria: small spike in auth latency for EU users due to longer auth roundtrip, adding 5s timeout fallback.

alex: ramping to 70% now per plan. If p99 > 1.5x baseline or error rate > 0.5% then rollback to previous weights.

devops-bot: change id 69c2: global rollout to target weights us-west-2 0.6 eu-west-1 0.4. Drain in progress.

jing: warm jobs completed, caches ~85% warmed for top keys.

leo: monitoring dashboards green besides expected latency bump. Cost alert threshold set to $500/hr for incremental egress — will notify.

sre-oncall: observed a handful of 503s during drain window. Small window, under alert threshold. Log sample: 
```
2026-02-03T10:12:45Z ERROR serve: request failed: OOM while executing forward pass for model gpt-medium
```

alex: flagged model teams to lower batch sizes temporarily for gpt-medium in ap-southeast to reduce OOMs.

maria: team confirms batch size -1 on ap-southeast routing table for gpt-medium.

devops-bot: alert: cost-monitor -> incremental egress $620/hr (threshold breached).

leo: finance pinged. We should consider shifting more weight to eu-west-1 to cut egress cost; but that will increase latency for NA users. Decision?

alex: keep current weights for 30m — product stakeholders ok for short window. If cost stays >$600/hr after 30m, shift additional 20% to eu-west-1.

sre-oncall: noted. I'll keep an eye on node churn in ap-southeast and continue reclaim attempts (drain failed pods, restart evicted nodes).

ops-bot: user-notification: incident update posted to #status (internal).

maria: metrics look stable after ramp. No new OOM patterns.

alex: leaving autoscale locked for 30m; scheduling follow-up postmortem. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

leo: closing the change in 40m unless we see regressions.

devops-bot: change id 69c2 marked stable.

sre-oncall: follow-up action items: 1) audit preemption events in ap-southeast, 2) validate node group scaling policies, 3) investigate scheduler settings that allowed aggressive compaction. Assigning to @jing and @sre-oncall.

alex: will open a postmortem ticket and include cost/time timeline + GLB decision log.

maria: thanks all.

ops-bot: incident severity lowered to S2.

leo: side note for later — consider adding region-aware cache pre-warming in the GLB control plane to reduce cold-start impact during shifts.
